You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data points to mid-2015. Unemployment is 5.3%, which matches roughly May–June 2015, and the fed funds rate is 0.14%, so the Fed had not yet hiked. Headline CPI is 0.18% year over year, which fits spring 2015. The dollar is up 15% year over year, which fits early to mid 2015. Gold is down 15% over 12 months, also consistent.

To narrow the month, I looked at the 2-year yield of 0.72% and the 10-year of 2.28%. The 10-year was about 2.3% in June 2015, and the 2-year was about 0.7%.

Other readings point the same way:
- Treasuries 20y+ returned +6.0% in the latest month, which suggests yields fell. That would fit a month such as February 2015, when yields rose and then fell, or July 2015.
- The 3-month change in the 10-year is +0.23, so yields were higher than three months earlier. The 12-month change is -0.30.
- In June 2014 the 10-year was about 2.6%, so a 12-month change of -0.30 gives roughly 2.3% now, which fits June 2015.
- The VIX is at 12.13, which is low. It was around 12 in July 2014, and about 13 in June 2015.
- Emerging-market equity fell 6.2% in the month and 13% over three months. A drop of that size fits August 2015 or so, but the 3-month figure of -13% is large.
- Gold fell 6.3% in the month, which fits July 2015.

The 20y+ Treasury return of +6.0% in one month does not fit June 2015, when yields rose. That points to July 2015 instead, or to January 2015, when long yields fell sharply, though January 2015 does not match the 10-year level.

I take the 12-month change in unemployment (-0.8) to mean it was 6.1% a year earlier, which fits June–July 2014 and so a snapshot of June–July 2015. The 3-month drop of -0.2 means it was 5.5% three months earlier, which fits March–April 2015, so the snapshot is likely June 2015.

However, 20y+ Treasuries up 6% in a month with the 10-year yield at 2.28% doesn't fit June either. In July 2015 the 10-year ended at 2.17%, and Treasuries gained about 2% in the month. In Jan 2015 the 10-year ended near 1.64%. Gold -6.3% fits July 2015 (gold fell about 6.8%). The CPI of 0.18% year over year fits June 2015 at 0.12% or July at 0.17%, and core of 1.77% fits July 2015 at 1.8%. The 10-year at 2.28% may reflect a mid-month figure.

I settle on July 2015.
